title.en: Read a recipe as a document: yield, allergens, steps, end conditions and a critical control point

goal.en: A Cookwala recipe is a typed document a class can read without any device: how much it makes, which allergens it carries, which operation each step is, and the measurable condition that ends it.

note.en: Kofta in the oven: four servings, no declared allergens, ten steps; the bake ends when the core probe reads 71 degC, a critical control point for ground meat.
Shakshuka declares eggs under both the EU and US allergen lists and may be scaled from half to double.
The number in the recipe is not arbitrary: the default limits pack has the same 71 degC minimum for ground meat, with its source.

outcome.en: You can show students where a safe temperature comes from and how a recipe states it as a condition a sensor can check. Next: scenario 036 looks at the knife-work rules in the vocabulary.
